APP_TAGLINE: A country risk index built from open data, with room for an analyst's judgment.
AUTHOR: Tuan Dung Nguyen
MONO_FONT: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

pillars.label: Political Stability & Violence
pillars.question: How likely is political violence, unrest or armed conflict to disrupt people and operations?

pillars.label: Governance & Institutions
pillars.question: Can people rely on institutions: courts, regulators, contracts, clean administration?

pillars.label: Macroeconomic & Financial
pillars.question: Is the economy exposed to a crisis: inflation, debt distress, balance-of-payments stress?

pillars.label: Social & Humanitarian Pressure
pillars.question: Are there social pressures that can turn into instability, such as joblessness or displacement?

indicators.label: Political stability & absence of violence
indicators.description: Perceptions of the likelihood of political instability and politically motivated violence, including terrorism. Higher score = more stable.

indicators.label: Battle-related deaths per 100,000 people
indicators.description: Deaths in state-based armed conflicts (UCDP definition), scaled by population. Countries with no recorded conflict are scored 0.

indicators.label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people
indicators.description: A proxy for criminal violence and the state's control over security.

indicators.label: Voice & accountability
indicators.description: Citizens' ability to choose their government; freedom of expression, association and media.

indicators.label: Government effectiveness
indicators.description: Quality of public services and the civil service, and the credibility of policy commitments.

indicators.label: Regulatory quality
indicators.description: Ability to formulate and implement sound policies that permit private-sector development.

indicators.label: Rule of law
indicators.description: Confidence in contract enforcement, property rights, the police and the courts.

indicators.label: Control of corruption
indicators.description: The extent to which public power is exercised for private gain, including state capture.

indicators.label: Inflation, average consumer prices
indicators.description: Current-year IMF estimate. High inflation erodes incomes and is a classic trigger of unrest.

indicators.label: Real GDP growth
indicators.description: Current-year IMF estimate. Recessions strain budgets, jobs and political support.

indicators.label: General government gross debt
indicators.description: Current-year IMF estimate. High debt limits room to respond to shocks.

indicators.label: Government net lending/borrowing
indicators.description: Current-year IMF estimate. Large deficits signal pressure for austerity or money printing.

indicators.label: Current account balance
indicators.description: Current-year IMF estimate. Persistent deficits create dependence on foreign financing.

indicators.label: Total reserves in months of imports
indicators.description: The buffer against a currency or balance-of-payments crisis. Under 3 months is a common warning line.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate
indicators.source: ILO modelled estimate via World Bank WDI
indicators.description: Share of the labour force without work (IMF estimate used where the ILO series is missing).

indicators.label: Youth unemployment (ages 15–24)
indicators.source: ILO modelled estimate via World Bank WDI
indicators.description: A well-documented driver of protest movements.

indicators.label: Forcibly displaced people from the country
indicators.description: Refugees, asylum seekers, others in need of international protection and internally displaced people originating from the country, as a share of its population.

RED_FLAGS: War-level violence (≥1,000 battle deaths in a year, UCDP threshold)
Active armed conflict (≥25 battle deaths in a year, UCDP threshold)
Thin FX reserves (<3 months of imports)

The traditional rule of thumb discussed in the IMF's reserve-adequacy work

Seismographic line: one person in twenty forcibly displaced
